summary_for_children: Al-'Adiyat means The Racers. It swears by racing horses and says people are often ungrateful.
environment_concept: At dawn, a line of horses gallops across the dunes, panting (100:1, 100:3); sparks fly where their hooves strike the stones (100:2) and clouds of dust rise behind them (100:4). The horses carry no riders; no person is shown.
architecture_and_scenery: Open dunes with a rocky stretch, galloping horses on a loop, spark and dust particles.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Charging Horses
story_library.children_narration: Surah Al-Adiyat begins with a powerful image of horses running at great speed. It then reminds us that human beings can become ungrateful and too attached to possessions. We should remember the blessings we have received.

world_idea.title: The Galloping Plains
world_idea.description: Observe beautifully animated horses in a windswept landscape, learn about their movement, and discover a reflective lesson about gratitude. ## Part 6 — Surahs 101–114

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The Quran says "the racers"; horses is the common tafsir reading. It is labelled as such.
